label: Snell's Window
blurb: Looks up at the shot from under water. Light from the whole sky above squeezes through the surface into a bright circle about 97 degrees across, worked out with Snell's law, so the middle of the picture sits overhead and everything near the horizon crowds into the rim. Outside the circle the surface turns into a mirror by total internal reflection and shows the dark water below. Every colour bends by its own amount, so the edge of the window carries a thin rainbow, and the waves, which move at the speed real water waves of that size move, wobble the circle and ripple the sky inside it. Depth and Murk soak up the red the way water does.
